title: Learn the Tap Shim Sham (How to)

method.teacher_system: The teacher introduces the history of the dance, demonstrates the steps slowly with spoken counts and rhythmic cues from a back-facing view, and then builds up speed while combining sections.
method.signature: Providing a continuous back-facing view of the feet and lower body throughout the entire tutorial so learners can mirror the movements effortlessly.

practices.what: Explains the first step using spoken counts and breaks down stomp-spank-step combinations starting on four.
Teaches the break step incrementally, explaining the rhythm and foot placements before combining it with previous steps.
Repeats the accumulated sequence multiple times to build muscle memory and clean up the rhythm.
Warns against common rhythmic errors and demonstrates the correct versus incorrect timing for the step.

adaptations.difficulty: Pushing on count four versus count one
adaptations.adjustment: Acknowledge different versions taught elsewhere and be prepared to do both.

beliefs.belief: The Shim Sham is a beautiful piece of historical choreography and repertoire that all tap dancers should have access to.
There are multiple versions of the Shim Sham in the world, and learners should be prepared to do both.

moments.says: The teacher introduces the Shim Sham as the tap dancer's national anthem and explains its historical background.
The teacher clarifies the distinction between a stamp and a full-foot step to correct form.
The teacher explains that different versions exist regarding when to push, preparing the learner for multiple variations.

mentor.what_stays: The teacher leaves the learner feeling equipped with historical repertoire and technical clarity.

struggles.theme: Writing down counts from the video
Building up speed on step one

clicked.theme: Focusing only on the feet makes it easy to follow

meant.theme: Helped revive tap dancing after many years away
Brought joy and fun during isolation or class suspensions

method.limits: Only the first 600 seconds of the video were analyzed; audio instructions are descriptive of lower body movements only.
